evaluator: E10 – Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), re-check of E8's findings on the build after fix round 3, persona: image-analysis specialist in a bioimaging core facility who writes Fiji macros and Python daily, cares about reproducibility, provenance and ImageJ-identical results, and has used napari, QuPath and Icy
method: I re-tested E8's six new problems (E8-1 … E8-6) and the twelve E7 items E8 left 'partly fixed' / 'not fixed', using E8's controls and sequences, then ran the regression pass the brief asks for. Nobody told me what was fixed and I read no source code, docs/USABILITY.md or other evaluators' files. Evidence: screenshots, DOM/ARIA facts, recorder lines, REST responses (/api/state, /api/recorder, /api/recorder/preview, /api/recorder/ijm, /api/script/run, all with my X-Lumen-Client header), Results/ROI counts and a TIFF tag dump. Tooling: one persistent headless Google Chrome (Playwright from the e2e venv, channel=chrome, swiftshader, 1440×900, host locale en_US with region DE), driven through a small local socket so one browser served the whole session; short viewport checks at 1000×800, 1280×800 and 1920×1080 used the same page. One second tab in the same browser was opened and closed again to see what a new tab's recorder shows. memory_pressure at the start: 58 % free. Start state: /api/state had 0 images, 0 ROIs, 0 results; File ▸ Close All from the menubar answered 'No images to close'. Walked: menubar by mouse (all eight menus, Open Sample / New / Export / Open Recent / Plugins ▸ Batch submenus) and keyboard (F10, arrows, Enter, Esc) at 1440 and 1000 px; File ▸ Open Sample ▸ Synthetic nuclei into the empty workspace; empty-state, palette and Command Reference counts; palette 'bleach'; per-channel display edits (DAPI max only, Auto, eye toggle, Viridis); Otsu threshold → Analyze Particles with Min size typed as '2,5'; Gaussian σ=500 → ⌘Z; Gaussian σ=1, Invert, Smooth, Median → History jump by keyboard; → IJM in the UI and via REST; Apply Recorded Macro to Folder sheet and /api/recorder/preview; page reload; a new tab; script editor ('lumen.', Ctrl+Space, Tab, large view); Plot Profile without selection and with an oval; T1 head → 3-D View large view; split view; Gaussian sheet '?' help and Command reference; '?' overlay; New Image 'timeseries' (256×256, 20 frames, noise) → Tracks wizard (auto threshold, 60, 84, radius '3,5'); Preferences; Set LUT sheet; full menu-label and palette-name scan; Blobs open/close by tab ×, tab switch, Z Project (on the time series and on T1 head), Invert, Smooth ×2; File ▸ Save As into eval_e10, Gaussian σ typed '1,5', ⌘S, TIFF tag dump (tifffile was not in the e2e venv; I used the project's .venv/bin/python -I only to read the file); ROI Manager and Results Clear → Undo clear and the batch preview / IJM afterwards; Median radius typed '0,25' and 'abc'; /api/script/run getuser/getcwd. Not covered: a real screen reader, several users at the same time, running a real folder batch. Clean-up: File ▸ Close All (menubar, 'Close without saving' for 4 images); ROI Manager (41) and Results (41) cleared through their confirmed Clear dialogs; my 'Particle Summary' table removed with lumen.session.tables.pop via /api/script/run because no UI showed it once the images were closed; both of my recorders cleared (DELETE /api/recorder for a6bc5657026a4e03 and c769f6fbb54c4abe); preferences and theme untouched; my Save did not add a Recent entry. Final /api/state: 0 images, 0 ROIs, 0 results, no tables. The browser and driver were closed; ps shows no Chrome or Playwright process of mine. saved_max_t1_e10.tif, tiff_tags.txt, recorder_evidence.json and menu_labels.json are kept next to this file as evidence.

regressions.heuristic: User control and freedom / Accessibility (keyboard operation)
regressions.observation: With the clipping fixed, keyboard navigation inside the menus broke. F10 focuses 'File' and ↓ (or Enter/Space) opens the menu (aria-expanded=true), but focus stays on the trigger. More ↓, Home or Enter never reach an item, and no item is highlighted. Tab leaves for the search box. ← / → move between top-level menus but focus stays on the trigger that was focused first. If a menu was opened with the mouse, ↓ does enter the items, → / ← open and close submenus, and Enter runs the item (Help ▸ Keyboard Shortcuts worked). But ← or → on a top-level item (to reach the neighbouring menu) shows that menu and drops focus to <body>; from there no key works, and Esc closes the menu with focus still on <body>. In E8, ↓ from the keyboard reached the items (they were only clipped visually), so keyboard-only and screen-reader users have lost the menus. ⌘K is the remaining keyboard route.

regressions.heuristic: Aesthetic and minimalist design / Help and documentation (regression of an E8 fix)

The Help menu now has 'Design & Research Notes', and opening Help ▸ Command Reference shows five tabs (README / Commands / Fiji parity / Design / Research). 'Design' opens 'Lumen — design notes … Fiji's documented UX problems … "Window soup" …' and 'Research' opens 'Scientific image-analysis GUIs: a sourced review for Lumen … Lumen re-implements the Fiji/ImageJ toolbox behind a single-window, keyboard-first UI (DESIGN.md)'. regressions.heuristic: Error prevention / Visibility of system status
regressions.location: Operation sheets' numeric fields (seen in Median ▸ Radius)
regressions.observation: Input that isn't a number is marked but not stopped. Out-of-range values get an inline message and a disabled Apply ('0,25' → 'radius must be between 0.5 and 1000'), but 'abc' or '2,5,1' only turn the field red (aria-invalid=true). There is no message and Apply stays enabled. Pressing Apply with 'abc' ran Median with radius=2.0, the default, which is not what the field showed. The recorder honestly writes radius=2.0, but the user believes they ran something else. A slipped key ('2,,5', '2.5.') silently gives a different filter size.
regressions.evidence: 54_median_bad_input.png, 55_median_abc.png; recorder after Apply: lumen.run("filters.median", radius=2.0, shape='disk', scope='slice').

regressions.observation: The new processing log is a big step forward but has two inaccuracies. The derivation line has no parameters ('Derived from: t1-head.tif ▸ Z Project', without 'Max Intensity, start=1, stop=10'), unlike the numbered steps ('4. Gaussian Blur (sigma=1.5, scaled_units=False)'). After Save As → Gaussian → ⌘S, the log gained 'Source: …/eval_e10/saved_max_t1_e10.tif', i.e. the file names itself as its source, while the real origin (the T1 head sample) only appears in the derivation line.

Back, detect again at 84 (1 spot) → step 2 still shows 60.01 in the threshold field and 'Quality ≥ 60.01: keeps ≈ 1 of 1 spots', while the histogram axis now runs 84.32–84.32 and the threshold marker sits off the histogram. The slider value is stale and below every detected spot, so 'Apply threshold' would apply a number that no longer means anything for this detection.
regressions.evidence: 48_tracks_step2_stale_threshold.png; wizard text before and after the second detection.

regressions.location: Image ▸ Stacks ▸ Z Project on a single-slice time series (20 frames)
regressions.observation: On the 20-frame 'timeseries' (z=1, t=20) the sheet pre-fills Start 1 / Stop 20, then Apply answers inside the sheet 'Z Project needs a stack with more than one slice'. Nothing is recorded or logged. An 'Axis Z / T' choice exists, but only under Advanced options, and the message doesn't point to it. Fiji projects a single-slice time series over its frames, so a max-intensity-over-time projection of a time-lapse (a daily task in a facility) fails the first time for every Fiji user.
regressions.evidence: 51_zproject_timeseries.png, 56_zproject_timeseries_advanced.png; /api/state log has no Z Project entry.

positives: The menubar is back: every menu and submenu opens fully with the mouse at 1000, 1280, 1440 and 1920 px, long submenus scroll inside the window, and Fiji's menu structure is browsable again.

The recorder survives a reload (client id in sessionStorage). The IJM export cancels undo pairs instead of writing run("Undo"), explains that in the script, and converts a max-only display change with getMinAndMax.
The folder batch finally leaves out what I undid, lists the undone commands by name, and says so in the summary.
Saved TIFFs now carry a processing log in the ImageJ Info property ('Derived from …', numbered steps with parameters) and Software 'Lumen 0.1.0'. Fiji's Show Info will display my provenance.
History rows show every parameter, defaults included, and display edits are History steps too.
Tracks detection now behaves like TrackMate's preview: only the current frame's spots on the image, nothing dumped into the shared ROI Manager, and add_to_manager=False recorded.
Numbers are shown with '.' everywhere, and a German keyboard's '2,5' is accepted and parsed in sheets and the Tracks wizard. Out-of-range values get an inline message and a disabled Apply.
Fiji vocabulary keeps improving: Bleach Correction exists with the three Fiji methods, Gaussian has 'Scaled units', sheet help names the ImageJ command, and the Command reference jumps to the row.
Accessibility moved forward again: per-channel names for Auto/Reset/Inv, a correct pressed-state eye toggle, named split-view selects, and focus handled in the large editor and the 3-D view.

Small polish that matters: one consistent command count (499), the first image fits the viewport, the recorder header fits the inspector, the Set LUT list is grouped, and the Close All dialog names the images with unsaved changes.
overall: Most of what I flagged after round 2 is fixed. Eleven of my 18 open items are fixed, six are narrower and one remains. The two blockers from E8 are gone: the menubar works with the mouse again, and the recorder survives a reload. The IJM export and the folder batch also finally handle undo correctly, and saved TIFFs carry a real processing log. For a single-user facility workstation I'd now hand Lumen to people who already use Fiji, with two warnings. First, the default batch list and the IJM export still replay ROI Manager and Results clears that I took back (E7-5), which can empty each file's ROIs and Results in a batch; anyone running a folder batch must read the command list before Apply. Second, a non-numeric entry in a sheet runs with the default value instead of stopping (E10-3). Keyboard-only users have lost the menus (E10-1) and must use ⌘K, and Fiji users will trip over Z Project refusing a time-lapse (E10-6). What still blocks a shared facility server is unchanged (E7-21): one set of preferences, ROI Manager, Results and recent files for everybody, the server's own file system in the Save dialog, and unrestricted Python as the server account. Fix the clear/restore pairing and the numeric validation, restore keyboard focus in the menus, and per-user separation is the last big step.
